new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress falls on the last syllable of the (suffixed) word, regardless of word class or length; stressed vowels are higher, higher-pitched and longer. Corroborated by Whaley/Grenoble/Li 1999 ('Word-level stress in most Oroqen dialects is fixed word final') and Lulich & Whaley 2012 ('For the large majority of Oroqen speakers, stress is word final.. regardless of word-class or length of the word').
new_statements.secondary_stress: Li 1996 (ch. 1, ~p. 20), reporting Zhang, Li & Zhang 1989: primary stress on the last syllable of the stem, secondary stress on the initial syllable. Li & Whaley 2012 (reduplication chapter snippet): each repeated syllable in suffix reduplication carries its own secondary stress, main stress on the stem. Whaley 2023 snippet does not mention secondary stress.
new_statements.exceptions: Li 1996: 86 for Baiyinna (Baiyina) Orochen: word stress 'basically' final, but weight-sensitive — 'if the syllables are equally heavy, stress falls on the final syllable, otherwise, stress falls on the last heavier syllable which may not be word final' (heavy = long vowel or short vowel + coda). Whaley & Li 2000: 123 fn. 13: the Northeastern dialect differs from the other dialects, 'where stress is fixed word-finally' (continuation not visible). Lulich & Whaley 2012: 'On a few occassions, we have found speakers who place stress on the..' (continuation not visible).
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (Whaley 2023 explicitly 'word level stress'; 'at the level of more complex utterances' follows, not visible). Elicited/citation forms; Lulich & Whaley 2012 is instrumental (3 speakers, Central and Northeastern dialects).
new_statements.identity_note: All sources describe the Oroqen/Orochen of China (oroq1238; ISO orh), not the Russian 'Orochon' varieties of Evenki. Dialects matter: Whaley 2023 and Lulich & Whaley 2012 generalise over Oroqen speakers (Central/Xunke, Northeastern, Kumarchen, Birarchen, Selpechen, Gankui); Li 1996: 86 describes Baiyinna (Baiyina, Huma county, Heilongjiang) Orochen with a weight-sensitive variant; Zhang, Li & Zhang 1989 is Xunke Oroqen; Whaley & Li 2000 say the Northeastern dialect differs from the word-final norm. The Evenki file in the folder (Bulatova & Grenoble 1999) is even1259, not the target.
